_comment: 🔮️ Test-only references of the 🎯️goals owner. `ajv` is already a devDependency of 🔨️modules/📚️library/📦️packages/🟦️typescript and is registered in the repository-root 🔒️dependencies.json; no production code of this module can reach it, and this module ships no TypeScript package at all.

productionDebt.plan: The same reach print's `ajv` oracle records: these packages declare ajv as a runtime dependency for verification code in scripts and helpers outside this module. This module's own production never imports ajv, so the oracle stays independent of the subject. The debt shrinks as those owners move validation behind the framework's own schema layer or onto the test platform. No path may join.

oracles.rationale: The fixtures are real 🎯️goal.json documents copied out of this repository's own goals tree, so the bytes a codec must reproduce were written by neither implementation. `ajv` is a real draft 2020-12 validator and decides whether each of those documents actually satisfies 🧬️schema/🔣️.json, so a schema that has drifted away from the Go and Rust decoders fails here instead of agreeing with itself; its JSON.parse/JSON.stringify pass is additionally a third, independently written serialiser of the same bytes, which is what makes the byte-for-byte re-encoding claim mean something.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: The `GOAL/SUBGOAL` path, the depth that decides whether a goal owns a milestone or an issue, and the 🎯️-tagged compose identifier are this repository's own conventions, defined by 🪪️identity's emoji table and by the goals module itself. No third party implements any part of them, so no reference can exist. The fixture freezes inputs only, including the real identifiers and compose identifiers in the repository's own goals tree, and confidence comes from two independently written implementations agreeing on depth, root, parent, filesystem form, composition from a title and the trailing number of a reference.

The goal/ticket forest is this repository's own presentation of its own two aggregates: which goal a goal hangs under is decided by the identifier prefix, siblings sort by due date with a blank date last, tickets nest under tickets, and tickets naming no known goal collect under a trailing `No Goal` node. Nothing outside this repository knows that shape. The scenario renders the structure with an implementation-owned line renderer rather than the entity vocabulary, so it judges the tree and not a presentation string, and confidence comes from two independently written implementations agreeing on the connectors, the order and the counts.

Opening, changing, closing, reopening and deleting a goal is this repository's own workflow over its own store and its own management provider; no third party has a goal aggregate to compare against. Every effect is a port with an in-memory implementation, so the scenario observes the whole outcome — the stored documents, the ordered provider calls, the emitted envelopes and the class of every refusal — rather than a return value, and confidence comes from two independently written implementations replaying the same script and agreeing on all four.
